headline: Supreme Infrastructure gets NCLT deadline extension to October 31 for ₹2,200 crore debt settlement
hook: Extension buys time for major lenders
summary: The National Company Law Tribunal in Mumbai has extended the payment deadline to October 31 for Supreme Infrastructure to settle its ₹2,200 crore debt. State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, and Union Bank of India have agreed on a framework to complete these settlement obligations. This extension provides the distressed infrastructure firm crucial breathing room to finalize repayment terms with its primary institutional creditors. Retail investors holding exposure to these public sector banks should note the ongoing resolution of legacy stressed assets.
whats_next: October 31 payment deadline for settlement completion
why_it_matters: Debt resolution progress clears legacy stress for lender banks.
winners_losers: Supreme Infrastructure gains / lenders clear bad loans

headline: Supreme Infrastructure gets more time from NCLT to settle Rs 2,200 crore debt
hook: Relief for lenders on a mountain of dues
summary: Supreme Infrastructure has received an extension of its payment deadline from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) to settle its mounting ₹2,200 crore debt. This extension gives the company additional breathing room to restructure its liabilities and avoid harsher insolvency proceedings. For Indian retail investors, resolution of large distressed debt burdens at infrastructure firms signals gradual asset recovery in the banking and construction sectors. While direct retail exposure to the stock is limited, successful debt resolution helps clean up stressed assets on lender balance sheets.
whats_next: Next debt repayment milestone as mandated by NCLT
why_it_matters: Stressed infrastructure debt resolution aids lender balance sheet cleanup

headline: Supreme Infrastructure India announces Scheme of Arrangement
hook: Routine corporate filing from Supreme Infrastructure
summary: Supreme Infrastructure India Limited has formally informed the stock exchange regarding a Scheme of Arrangement. The company did not disclose the specific financial details or structural purpose of the arrangement in this initial disclosure. Such schemes typically involve mergers, demergers, or restructuring of company assets. Retail investors holding the stock should monitor subsequent filings for concrete details on how this restructuring impacts shareholder value.
whats_next: Company disclosure with Scheme of Arrangement details
why_it_matters: Awaiting filing details to assess impact on share value.

headline: Supreme Infrastructure India schedules 43rd AGM for November 12
hook: Annual meeting scheduled for Supreme Infrastructure
summary: Supreme Infrastructure India has announced that its 43rd Annual General Meeting will be held on November 12. The company has set November 6 as the start date for the book closure period. This process is a standard procedural requirement for listed companies to finalize the list of shareholders eligible for voting and dividends.
why_it_matters: Routine procedural update with no direct impact on share price.

headline: Supreme Infrastructure sets 43rd AGM for November 2026
hook: Routine procedural filing from Supreme Infrastructure
summary: Supreme Infrastructure India Limited has scheduled its 43rd Annual General Meeting for November 12, 2026. The meeting will be conducted virtually through video conferencing or other audio-visual means. Retail investors holding the stock should note the corporate event date. Such routine AGM notices do not impact the company's financial fundamentals.
why_it_matters: No financial impact for retail investors.

headline: Supreme Infrastructure gets extension to hold AGM
hook: AGM delayed for small-cap infrastructure firm
summary: Supreme Infrastructure India Limited has received approval from the Registrar of Companies in Mumbai to extend its Annual General Meeting deadline. The company now has until November 15, 2026, to hold the AGM for the financial year ending March 31, 2026. The extension grants an additional one month and 15 days beyond the standard timeline. For retail investors, delayed AGMs can indicate administrative backlogs or reporting delays within financially distressed micro-cap companies.
why_it_matters: Routine compliance delay for a distressed micro-cap company.
